title: Isabella Guzman
text:
Isabella Guzman playing soccer for Denison University





Hi Dr. Love! I’m Isabella, a graduate student in the MS in Biostatistics program at Case Western Reserve University. I am on the accelrated track within the biostatistics program so I plan on being completed with my masters in August 2027. I graduated from Denison University in May 2026 with a BA in Global Health and a minor in Spanish. Having the opportunity to go to Denison was the bigget blessing of my life. The liberal arts education and environment i absolutely thrived in. I met some of my best friends there and encountered a lot of failures that changed me into someone I am incredibly proud to be. I actually applied to CWRU as a senior in highschool and did not get in. While I was devastated, looking back at it now I realized that not getting in the first time was the single biggest blessing of my life. I learned failure was a blessing and not a setback. I walked onto the soccer team at Denison and played three incredible years there. Every NCAA athlete has 4 years of eligibility to use, so with one more left I decided to try my luck at Case again. This time I was successful, but if I decided to give up in the beginning I would have never been here. Honestly, being a student at this school is my proudest achievement. I view failure as a forever motivator as opposed to something that gives me sadness. Currently I am honing in on my skills in R, Quarto, and health care analytics, and I’m especially interested in using data to understand community health needs and overall disease trends. I’m also a member of the CWRU women’s soccer team, and when I am out of season I hope to be more involved in the Case community.

title: Isabella Guzman
text:
Soccer
Soccer has been a big part of my life as a player and as a youth coach. I have been playing since I was 2 years old. My dad was a semi-professional player in Spain and in Europe. His love of the game was passed onto me from an early childhood. Aside from my collegiant career in the United States, I also followed in my dads footsteps in the spring 2025. While studying abroad, I had the opportunity to play semi-professional soccer for CD Toledo feminino for the remainder of their season. It was an incredible experience and we ended up winning the title for our division and secured promotion from the fourth division to the third division of Spanish soccer.
